summary: Vishva Bandhu (1897–1973) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He served as Founder-Principal of Dayanand Brahma Mahavidyalaya (1921), Director at Dayanand Anglo-Vedic College (1934), and Director of the Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute (~1924–1973).

Vishvanath Narayan Mandlik (1833–1899) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Elphinstone College (~1847–1851). He served as an examiner at the University of Mumbai and as Vice-President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1878).

Vishwa Nath Pathak (1926–2003) worked in Indology and history/archaeology, studying under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He served as a professor at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (attested 1973–1978 and 1987).

Vishwanath Prasad Varma (born 1924) is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied under Dhirendra Mohan Datta (~1942–1946), Ganga Nath Bhattacharya (~1942–1946), doctoral supervisor Kali Kinkar Datta (~1948–1950), and Joachim Wach (1950).

Vishwanathan Venkatachalam (1925–2002) was an Indologist educated at the University of Madras, RTM Nagpur University, and Vikram University. He served as Director of Scindia Oriental Institute (~1972–1985) and vice-chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1986–1989, 1992–1995).

Vitus Angermeier is an Indologist who studied under MA supervisor Karin Preisendanz (until 2007), Chlodwig H. Werba, and Roque Mesquita. He is attested as a lecturer at the University of Vienna in 2026.

Vladimir Balabushevich (1900–1970) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He served as Head of the Indian Department at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (attested 1970 and 1990).

Vladimir Minorsky (1877–1966) was an Iranian and Central Asian history/archaeology scholar. Educated at Moscow Imperial University (~1896–1900) and the Lazarev Institute of Oriental Languages (~1900–1903), he held posts at INALCO (~1923–1932) and SOAS University of London (~1932–1944).

Vladimir Tikhonov (born 1973) is a historian and scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Saint Petersburg State University, Moscow State University, and Korea University, he held posts at Kyung Hee University (1997–2000) and the University of Oslo (since 2000).

Volker Caumanns is a Tibetologist who earned his MA at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and his PhD at the University of Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard. He held posts at Munich (2006–2012) and LIRI (2012–2015).

Volker Grabowsky (born 1959) is a historian educated at Kiel University (~1978–1986) and Chiang Mai University (~1989–1990). He held posts at the University of Passau, National University of Laos, University of Münster (1999), and University of Hamburg (from 2009).

Volker Zotz (born 1956) is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Vienna (~1977–1986) and under Anagarika Govinda. He held academic posts at Vienna, Otani University, Ryukoku University, Saarland University, and the University of Luxembourg.

Vrajavallabha Dvivedi (1926–2012) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He headed the Yogatantra Department at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and served as Deputy Director at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1990–1992).
Vriti Sharma is an Indology and computational studies scholar who has held posts at the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi and BharatGen.
W. F. Jayasuriya was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under teachers Rerukane Ariyaratne, H. D. Dharmasiriwardhana, and M. U. Sri Kaveeswara.

W. H. D. Rouse (1863–1950) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Cheltenham College, Regent's Park College, and Cambridge. He held teaching posts at Bedford, Cheltenham, Rugby, and served as headmaster at The Perse School (1902–1928).

W. H. R. Rivers (1864–1922) was a medical and historical scholar educated at University of London and St Bartholomew's Hospital. He held posts at UCL, Cambridge, St John's College, and served as president of the Anthropological Society of London (~1921–1922).

W. Norman Brown (1892–1975) was an Indologist and historian who earned his PhD at Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield. He held posts at Johns Hopkins, SPMR College of Commerce, and served as Professor at the University of Pennsylvania (~1926–1966).

W. Randolph Kloetzli is a scholar of religion, Indology, and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (1964) under J. A. B. van Buitenen and others. He taught at American University, George Washington University, and Dartmouth College.

W. S. Karunatillake worked in linguistics and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1997) and as Visiting Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard University in 1998.
